daily_brief: The day's news is dominated by a major Microsoft outage affecting Outlook, Teams, and Copilot services across 74 countries, disrupting businesses, governments, and healthcare systems for over 12 hours [BBC, RFI, Globe and Mail]. Microsoft has attributed the incident to server overload rather than cyberattack, with services showing gradual recovery by Friday afternoon. In parallel, the fallout from former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation continues to escalate, with US lawmakers summoning him to testify before Congress over his alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy [BBC, France 24, Financial Times]. The scandal has wiped $550 billion from Nvidia's market value and raised serious questions about potential technology transfers to China. On the diplomatic front, US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met with both Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelensky, announcing that European delegates will be included in future Ukraine peace talks [BBC, RFI, Le Monde]. However, EU officials remain cautious, with foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas warning against Russian 'traps' that could divert focus from achieving a ceasefire [The Hindu]. Meanwhile, the IAEA expressed growing concern over Iran's undisclosed nuclear facility in Isfahan, warning of 'serious proliferation concerns' [BBC, The Hindu].

top_stories.headline: Global Microsoft Outage Disrupts Businesses and Governments Across 74 Countries
bullets: Microsoft 365 services including Outlook, Teams, and Copilot experienced outages beginning Thursday evening, affecting over 430 million potential users across 74 countries
Microsoft attributed the disruption to higher-than-usual server load, ruling out malicious activity or cyberattack
The outage forced some organizations to revert to fax machines, delayed train ticket retrieval in Germany, UK, and Canada, and caused 'serious impact' on the UK's National Health Service
By Friday afternoon, Microsoft reported gradual stabilization and extended email timeout windows to 48 hours to protect delayed messages

top_stories.headline: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Summoned to Congress Over Alleged Affair with Suspected Chinese Spy
bullets: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on Thursday after 33 years following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect of spying for China
Senate Banking Committee Chair Tim Scott summoned both Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify in December, with subpoena threatened if voluntary appearance is declined
Nvidia has lost $550 billion in market value over five days since the scandal broke
Bloomberg reported that a Chinese company founded by Alice Huang obtained banned Nvidia H800 chips, raising concerns about circumvention of US export restrictions

top_stories.headline: US Envoys Announce European Inclusion in Ukraine Peace Talks After Meeting Putin and Zelensky
bullets: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met with Putin in Moscow and Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday as part of shuttle diplomacy following inconclusive Abu Dhabi talks
Both sides agreed to include European Union delegates in future negotiations, with Zelensky stating Europeans will have 'a voice' in talks
Russia and Ukraine agreed to their largest prisoner exchange since the 2022 invasion, though details remain undisclosed
Putin maintained Russia's territorial demands have not changed, while EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas warned against Russian 'traps' that could divert focus from achieving a ceasefire

top_stories.headline: IAEA Warns of 'Serious Proliferation Concern' Over Undisclosed Iranian Nuclear Facility
bullets: The IAEA reported it is 'increasingly concerned' about a uranium enrichment plant in Isfahan that Iran announced one day before US-Israeli strikes began in June 2025
The agency does not know the exact location of the facility or whether it contains nuclear material, as inspectors have been barred since the conflict began
Before the June 2025 strikes, Iran had accumulated an estimated 441kg of uranium enriched to 60%, close to weapons grade, exceeding the 2015 nuclear deal limits
The IAEA urged Iran to take 'incremental steps' to allow inspectors to return, warning the situation 'needs to be rectified with the utmost urgency'

top_stories.headline: Ebola Outbreak in Congo Becomes Second-Deadliest in History as Rebel Violence Hampers Response
bullets: The Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has infected over 11,100 people and killed more than 5,430 in six months, making it the second-largest outbreak in history
Islamist rebels killed 66 civilians including three health workers and destroyed three clinics in Cantine-Aloya last week, with attacks continuing through Wednesday
Health workers report shortages of basic supplies including phones, fuel, and water, while violence is scattering Ebola-exposed people across wide areas
Early signs suggest a Canadian-developed vaccine designed for a different Ebola strain may be effective against the Bundibugyo virus causing this outbreak
